title: 2026 UK ETS installation permit surrender-revocation QA controls

sources.title: UK ETS for installations: how to comply

facts.fact: After an installation ceases operation, the operator must apply through METS to surrender the permit by the relevant surrender date or a later date agreed with the regulator.
Where the regulator gives a cessation notice, the relevant surrender date is one month from that notice.
Otherwise the surrender date includes one month from the date the installation ceased operation.
The alternative date includes one month from when the operator no longer intends authorised regulated activities to resume.
An operator may apply to surrender once all regulated activities have ceased even before surrender becomes obligatory.
Restarting regulated activity after surrender requires re-applying so a permit is in force before restart.
The regulator may revoke a permit for non-compliance or failure to pay a subsistence fee where applicable.
The regulator must revoke a permit where surrender is required and the operator fails to apply on time.
A surrender or revocation notice contains requirements the operator must comply with.
The notice includes reporting emissions up to its effective date and surrendering allowances equal to those reportable emissions.

guard_patterns.rule: Keep discretionary and mandatory revocation distinct.
Do not treat application as effective notice.
Do not confuse allowance obligation with measured emissions methodology.
